current.text: Verify that passwords are stored using an approved, computationally intensive, key derivation function (also known as a "password hashing function"), with parameter settings configured based on current guidance. The settings should balance security and performance to make brute-force attacks sufficiently challenging for the required level of security.

master.text: Verify that passwords are stored using an approved, computationally intensive, key derivation function (also known as a "password hashing function"), with parameter settings configured based on current guidance. The settings should balance security and performance to make brute-force attacks sufficiently challenging for the required level of security.

predecessors.text: Verify that passwords are stored in a form that is resistant to offline attacks. Passwords SHALL be salted and hashed using an approved one-way key derivation or password hashing function. Key derivation and password hashing functions take a password, a salt, and a cost factor as inputs when generating a password hash. ([C6](https://owasp.org/www-project-proactive-controls/#div-numbering))

Verify that if PBKDF2 is used, the iteration count SHOULD be as large as verification server performance will allow, typically at least 100,000 iterations. ([C6](https://owasp.org/www-project-proactive-controls/#div-numbering))

Verify that if bcrypt is used, the work factor SHOULD be as large as verification server performance will allow, with a minimum of 10. ([C6](https://owasp.org/www-project-proactive-controls/#div-numbering))
Verify password credential recovery does not reveal the current password in any way. ([C6](https://owasp.org/www-project-proactive-controls/#div-numbering))

summaries.body:
ASVS 5.0.0 V11.4.2 is merged from 4.0.3 password-storage controls in Authentication. V2.4.1 required passwords to be stored resistant to offline attacks, salted and hashed with an approved one-way KDF or password hashing function that takes password, salt, and a cost factor. V2.4.3 set a PBKDF2 iteration floor (typically at least 100,000, as large as the verifier allows). V2.4.4 set a bcrypt work-factor floor (minimum 10). The mapping also lists V2.5.3 (credential recovery must not reveal the current password) as covered; that recovery clause is not the current storage sentence.

On 2019-02-15 kisasondi reworded V2.4.1 in a “Password length proposed change” commit; on 2019-02-26 another V2.4.1 update followed. On 2019-02-25 vanderaj moved V2.4.4 while removing untestable L1 items. Issue #385 (ossie-git, 2019-02-05) is general V2 authentication feedback, not this hashing clause. Mapping and V2.4.1/2.4.3/2.4.4 are the reliable origin; files/SSRF git on the 5.0 slot is noisy.

In 5.0 the algorithm-specific PBKDF2 iteration count and bcrypt work-factor floors were collapsed into one requirement: an approved, computationally intensive KDF (“password hashing function”) with parameters set from current guidance, balancing security and performance so brute-force remains hard enough. Named 100,000 / work-factor-10 numbers are gone. The mapping also claims coverage of V2.5.3 recovery wording, which the current clause does not carry.

Number-formatting and CWSS-column commits on V2.5.3 are omitted. Files and SSRF events on this ID did not rewrite password hashing.
